result: No current release blocker found in this integration slice.

staticChecks.subdirectoryReferenceURLChecks: Root and /toolbox/ bases resolve correctly; all actual local targets exist
staticChecks.mirrorSHA256: All 27 manifest file hashes matched current bytes
staticChecks.retainedHeaders: All 23 CyberChef source headers retain original authors and Apache-2.0 license; Esolang Park MIT license retains 2021 Nilay Majorwar notice
staticChecks.buildIncludesResources: build.mjs copies public recursively to dist; normal build never runs maintenance fetch

reviewConclusions: content.js validates one canonical capability per article, unique IDs, section-bound citations and worked examples before registry/DOM work. Frozen nested data prevents accidental in-place changes.

createRegistry validates exact same-group visible owners and rejects missing lessons. Paired inverse directions retain one article owner; older operation directions continue to resolve through canonical capability aliases.
All 40 former article IDs map to existing precise articles; compatibility aliases are not duplicate inventory entries.
ReferenceList uses text-only components and safe links with noopener/noreferrer; actual leading-slash logical asset paths resolve against import.meta.url at the application root, including /toolbox/.
Knowledge examples use DataList with literal textContent and pre-wrap; they neither interpret code/HTML nor mutate the tool input/result state.
The knowledge reader handles stale asynchronous related-tool loads with revision guards and disconnect cleanup; it keeps current reader nodes on canonical route re-entry.
Mirrored docs link both upstream originals and precise license text. Hash manifests cover copies and notices; original runtime/vendor artifacts remain separate.

nonBlockingMaintenanceFindings.locator: fetch(): target.exists() and relative in old_hashes cache branch
nonBlockingMaintenanceFindings.issue: Cache reuse validates existing bytes against old SHA only, without checking old_manifest.commit or the per-file source_url against current COMMIT/remote. A future coordinated PIN and source-link upgrade could reuse old bytes while emitting source_url for the new commit.
nonBlockingMaintenanceFindings.currentRelease: Current source docs and runtime PIN both use 8cd426dd4f40f1423912d5fad91b578a86a65112 and current hashes match; no inaccurate current pin found.
nonBlockingMaintenanceFindings.suggestedFix: Reuse cached source only when old manifest pin and that file source_url match current expected remote. Otherwise fetch newly pinned bytes and then hash.
nonBlockingMaintenanceFindings.validation: 9 isolated Node/Python AST tests pass; actual predicate and fetch exercised with temporary files and stub-only urllib. No importer entrypoint, network or corpus rewrite executed.

limitations: No long browser suite or full verify rerun, per freeze instruction; root is running that separately.
This read-only check covers integration mechanics and current files, not a fresh semantic re-audit of every external document.
External access and Chinese carrier connectivity are not guaranteed by HTTP/url syntax checks.
No project files modified; this report is the only new file written under /tmp.
